title: Manual page
description: One record per Manual page. Holds everything that is constant across the chunks cut from it, so those fields are stored once and joined rather than copied onto every chunk.

part_id.description: From the sidebar nav tree ONLY. Never inferred from the URL slug — slugs collide across Parts (32A.2.3 and 32B.2.3 share one, distinguished by a trailing '1').

nav_title.description: As it appears in the sidebar.

examples: 22.1. Registrability under section 41 of the Trade Marks Act 1995

printed_page_ref.description: The page_ref this page's own <h1> prints, on the two pages where that is not its page_ref, and null on the other 498. 'page_ref' comes from the nav and must, because the nav is the only reliable source of Part membership — but TMM/Part20/3 prints 'Part 20.2. Definition of sign' while TMM/Part20/2 prints '20.2. Background to definition of a trade mark', so two pages claim 20.2. That is the Manual's defect and rule 1 says to record an ambiguity rather than resolve it: the nav still decides the address, and this says the page disagrees. Without it a bare 'part 20.2' resolves to one of them with nothing suggesting it might have meant the other.

content_hash.description: Whole-page hash. Cheap gate for the crawler: unchanged page, skip chunking entirely.

archived.description: The page carries the Manual's 'This page has been archived.' banner. It keeps its nav entry, its title and its amendment history, and has no prose left, so it yields no chunks. Distinct from retirement, which is a page leaving the nav altogether and moving to pages/_retired/.

images.description: Every image in the page's content, de-duplicated and sorted by (src, alt). Eight pages of the Manual are ONLY an image — a flowchart, a cross-search class table, the format of a summons — and they yield no chunks because there is no text in them. Without this they are indistinguishable from a page with nothing on it. The image bytes are not stored: this records that the image is there, and where.

src.description: Exactly as written in the source, which today is always root-relative ('/sites/default/files/trademark/image/...'). Resolving it against the site root is the consumer's join to make; rewriting it here would be a transformation this record cannot afford.

alt.description: null means the element carried no alt attribute; "" means it carried an empty one, which is how HTML spells 'decorative'. The difference is the entire content of 'Accessibility fix – alternative text for images', one of the Manual's own amendment reasons on 28 pages, so the two must not be collapsed.

last_amended.description: Most recent date in the page's 'Amended Reasons' table.

amendment_note.description: IP Australia's own words for the most recent change — 'Minor updates.', 'Update hyperlinks'. Lets a reviewer separate substantive practice change from cosmetic edits without reading the diff.

extractor_version.description: When this changes, chunks may need rebuilding even though the source text did not.
